request: Add two click buttons with the height of 2 millimetre to provide a comfortable and responsive feel for the user

actions.operation: Create/add two click-button features (quantity: 2) as new geometry

parameters.placement_region: Upper ergonomic shell, forward/nose side of wheel opening
parameters.layout_rule: Mirror about midplane between left and right side skins
parameters.button_perimeter_shape: Rounded-rectangle / ergonomic spline footprint (projected onto top shell)
parameters.edge_comfort: Apply edge fillets to button perimeters (typ. 0.5–1.0 mm, confirm)
parameters.button_separation: Maintain a center split/gap between buttons (typ. 0.8–1.2 mm, confirm)

actions.target: Main body (SOLID 0) top exterior surface; create two raised click zones on either side of the wheel opening without interfering with the wheel pocket/opening
actions.relational_constraint: Buttons shall have a height of 2 mm; buttons shall be symmetric left/right about the housing midplane; buttons shall not intersect the wheel opening boundary on the top shell and shall preserve clearance to the pocket walls
actions.unresolved_reference: Exact button footprint dimensions (length/width), exact front-to-wheel spacing, exact gap width between left/right buttons, whether buttons should be separate solids (moving parts) versus sculpted regions of the same solid, and final edge radii/softness targets for feel.
steps: Define datums for robust placement: create a midplane between the left and right side skins (between S3 left flank surface face_code 0007 / Brep FACE 7 and S4 right flank surface face_code 0010 / Brep FACE 10). This midplane will be the symmetry reference for the two buttons.

Identify the button placement region on the upper shell: use S1 main top shell face_code 0006 / Brep FACE 6 (the BSPLINE face containing the wheel opening inner loop). From the multiviews, place the buttons on the forward/nose side of the wheel opening on this same top face, so the wheel remains centered between the two click zones.

Create a sketch on a stable construction plane: create a plane approximately parallel to the global Top view (screen top view plane) passing through the top shell near the wheel opening area. If needed, define it as an offset plane above the highest point of face 0006 so the sketch can be projected downward onto the curved surface.

In the sketch, draw the button split line and footprints: (1) draw a centerline coincident with the midplane projection; (2) draw one button perimeter on one side of the centerline as a rounded rectangle or ergonomic spline; (3) mirror the perimeter across the centerline to create the second button; (4) enforce a controlled gap between the two perimeters along the centerline (target 0.8–1.2 mm, to be confirmed) so two distinct buttons are readable and feel separate.

Constrain the sketch relative to existing features: reference the wheel opening position by projecting/using the wheel opening edges on face 0006 (inner loop of face 0006) as construction geometry; keep the rear edges of the button perimeters offset away from the wheel opening boundary to avoid weakening the opening rim. Also keep the perimeters within the top shell boundary and away from the rear crown patch transition (S1 face_code 0005 / Brep FACE 5).

Project/Wrap the button perimeters onto the curved top face: project the two closed button loops from the sketch plane onto S1 face_code 0006 (use ‘Project to surface’, ‘Wrap/Emboss’, or equivalent). This creates two curves lying on the BSPLINE top surface.

Split the top face into button regions: perform a ‘Split Face’ operation on S1 face_code 0006 using the projected curves so that two distinct face regions (left button area and right button area) are created on the top shell surface.

Create the 2 mm button height by surface offset: apply an ‘Offset Face / Move Face’ outward along the local surface normals for each of the two split button face regions by +2.0 mm. This yields two raised click-button pads that follow the original shell curvature and meet the requested height.

Blend for comfort and responsiveness: apply fillets (or variable radius fillets where needed) along the perimeter edges created by the split/offset to remove sharp transitions and improve tactile feel (typ. 0.5–1.0 mm radius, to be confirmed). Ensure fillets do not roll into the wheel opening boundary on face 0006.

Check interference/clearance with the wheel pocket: verify the raised regions do not intrude into the wheel opening/pocket features (S6 pocket faces 0000/0002/0003/0004/0001; Brep FACE 0/2/3/4/1). If the offset causes any self-intersections near the opening rim, reduce footprint rearward, reduce local fillet radii, or add a local relief by trimming the button perimeter further from the opening edge.

Optional refinement if a visible split is desired: instead of (or in addition to) a sketch gap, create a shallow center groove by projecting a narrow slot curve along the midplane onto face 0006 and performing a shallow cut/offset-in (e.g., 0.3–0.6 mm) to visually and tactually separate the two click buttons while keeping the button top surfaces raised by 2 mm.

intention: Provide a comfortable and responsive feel for the user when clicking/pressing the buttons
Create two distinct left/right click zones symmetrically positioned around the existing scroll wheel opening without compromising wheel clearance or the top shell’s structural continuity
